harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created the opsbot account on both node1 and node2 (Alpine Linux), generated an ed25519 keypair as opsbot on node1, installed the public key into opsbot's authorized_keys on node2, and enforced key-only SSH authentication for opsbot on both nodes via a `Match User opsbot` sshd_config block (PasswordAuthentication no, KbdInteractiveAuthentication no, AuthenticationMethods publickey) plus a password-less shadow entry. Verified opsbot@node1 can run commands as opsbot@node2 over SSH using the key, and that password-based login for opsbot is rejected on both nodes. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured boot_id baselines, restarted node1 then node2 one at a time (native `reboot`), confirmed changed boot_id on each, and re-verified sshd status, account/key state, sshd config, and the live cross-node SSH command execution after both restarts.
actions_performed: Inspected OS/sudo state on node1 and node2 (Alpine 3.23)
Created opsbot user on node1 and node2 via adduser -D
Verified/created locked password entries; created /home/opsbot/.ssh (0700) on both nodes
Generated ed25519 keypair as opsbot on node1 (/home/opsbot/.ssh/id_ed25519)
Installed opsbot's public key into node2 /home/opsbot/.ssh/authorized_keys (0600)

Discovered sshd's locked-account ('!') shadow entry blocks pubkey auth too; changed shadow password field to '*' on both nodes to disable password auth without triggering sshd's account-lock rejection
Added 'Match User opsbot' block to /etc/ssh/sshd_config on both nodes requiring publickey-only auth; validated with sshd -t; reloaded sshd on both nodes
Verified opsbot@node1 -> opsbot@node2 SSH command execution succeeds with the key
Verified password-based SSH attempts for opsbot are rejected on both nodes (server offers only publickey)
Checked auth logs on node2 confirming 'Accepted publickey for opsbot' and rejection of password-only attempt
Captured boot_id/uptime/service baseline on both nodes

Restarted node1 via `reboot` (backgrounded so ack returned before disconnect), polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, verified sshd/account/config/key state, and re-tested opsbot cross-node SSH
Restarted node2 via `reboot`, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, verified sshd/account/authorized_keys/config state
Final end-to-end verification: opsbot@node1 executes a remote command as opsbot@node2 post-restart

evidence.requirement: opsbot account created on node1 (and node2, needed for the SSH target)
evidence.summary: adduser created opsbot on both nodes with locked/no-password shadow entries and 0700 .ssh directories

evidence.requirement: opsbot has SSH key-based access to run commands as opsbot on node2
evidence.summary: Generated ed25519 keypair as opsbot on node1, installed the public key in node2's opsbot authorized_keys, and successfully ran whoami/hostname/id as opsbot on node2 via SSH from node1 (before and after restart)

evidence.requirement: Key-based authentication required for opsbot on both systems (password auth rejected)
evidence.summary: sshd_config on both nodes has a Match User opsbot block requiring AuthenticationMethods publickey; config validated with sshd -t and reloaded; explicit password-only SSH attempts against opsbot on both nodes were rejected with Permission denied (publickey); auth log on node2 shows Accepted publickey for opsbot alongside the rejected password-only attempt

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id b83fd7ec...; issued backgrounded reboot with ack returned; node unreachable during reboot; boot_id changed to c386409c... on return; sshd active, opsbot account/key/sshd config intact, and cross-node SSH to node2 functional post-restart

evidence.requirement: Node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id 5e3bb0d6...; issued backgrounded reboot with ack returned; node unreachable during reboot; boot_id changed to 8cd8ce3d... on return; sshd active, opsbot account/authorized_keys/sshd config intact, and final cross-node SSH command from node1 as opsbot succeeded
